oauth_setup.desktop_native_app_flow: Google supports a dedicated OAuth flow for installed (native/desktop) apps. Unlike web server apps, native apps cannot keep client secrets. The flow requires PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange), with S256 recommended. The app opens the system browser for user consent and listens on a local loopback redirect URI (http://127.0.0.1:port) to receive the authorization code. The app then exchanges the code for access and refresh tokens at https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token. Custom URI schemes are no longer supported on Android/Chrome. Loopback redirect is DEPRECATED for mobile (Android, iOS) but supported for macOS, Linux, Windows desktop. Out-of-band (OOB) manual copy/paste redirect is deprecated and removed.
oauth_setup.loopback_redirect_rules: Supported for macOS, Linux, Windows desktop apps at http://127.0.0.1:port or http://[::1]:port. App must start an HTTP listener on a random available port. Redirect URI must exactly match one authorized in the Cloud Console Clients page. DEPRECATED for mobile (Android, iOS) — mobile apps should use Google Sign-In SDK or AppAuth.
oauth_setup.refresh_token_behavior: Refresh tokens are always returned for installed apps. Valid until user revokes access or token expires (time-based access). Refresh tokens can be used to obtain new access tokens without user interaction (offline access). Limits exist on number of refresh tokens per client/user. Old refresh tokens stop working if too many are issued. Time-based refresh tokens expire after the granted duration (refresh_token_expires_in field).
oauth_setup.consent_screen_testing_vs_production: Testing: 'unverified app' warning displayed during testing with sensitive/restricted scopes. Test users can be added in the Cloud Console to bypass verification warnings during development (up to 100 test users). Production: App must complete verification before sensitive/restricted scopes are available to general users. Consent screen must be configured with app name, support email, logo, privacy policy URL, and authorized domains.
oauth_setup.external_vs_internal_app_mode: External: Available to any Google Account. Requires app verification for sensitive/restricted scopes. Consent screen shows full app details. Internal: Only available to users within the same Google Workspace / Cloud Identity organization. Does not require verification. Users must belong to the organization. Internal apps bypass granular permissions consent in some cases.
oauth_setup.verification_triggers: App verification is triggered when the app requests: (a) sensitive scopes — requires brand verification and scope justification; (b) restricted scopes — requires independent security assessment (annual recertification), demonstrated need, and compliance with restricted scope requirements. Verification is NOT required for: non-sensitive scopes only, or internal-only apps, or apps using only test users.

verification_matrix.non_sensitive_verification: No verification required. App can be used immediately by any user. Includes scopes like userinfo.email, userinfo.profile, openid.
verification_matrix.sensitive_verification: Requires brand verification and scope justification. Google reviews app name, logo, privacy policy, and why each sensitive scope is needed. Processing time: typically days to weeks.
verification_matrix.restricted_verification: Requires independent security assessment (annual recertification). Must demonstrate that the app complies with restricted scope requirements. Additional requirements include: data use disclosure, demonstrated need with minimal scope, and compliance with API user data policy. Processing time: weeks to months. Includes scopes like gmail.readonly, calendar.readonly, drive.readonly, contacts.readonly.
verification_matrix.security_assessment_triggers: Required for restricted scopes. Must be performed by a Google-approved assessor (e.g., Leviathan, Bishop Fox). Annual recertification. Cost: varies (typically $15,000-$75,000+ per assessment). This means restricted-scope access is effectively enterprise-only for Rig Relay.

domain_wide_delegation.setup_requirements: 1) Create a service account in Google Cloud Console. 2) Generate a JSON key pair for the service account. 3) A Workspace super administrator must authorize the service account in the Admin console (Security > API Controls > Domain Wide Delegation), entering the service account's numeric Client ID and comma-separated OAuth scopes. 4) The app uses the service account key to create a JWT (RS256), which is exchanged for an access token. 5) The app specifies the user to impersonate via the 'sub' claim in the JWT or .with_subject() in client libraries.

security_constraints.token_transport: Access tokens must be sent in the Authorization: Bearer header. Query string parameter (access_token=) is possible but discouraged because URLs appear in server logs. The HTTP header is the recommended, safer method.
security_constraints.refresh_token_storage: Must be stored in secure, long-lived storage accessible across application invocations. Loss of refresh token requires full re-authentication. Only one active refresh token per client/user combination. Limit of 50-100 refresh tokens per user across all clients. Store encrypted, never log, never version-control.
security_constraints.incremental_authorization: NOT supported for installed apps (native/desktop). The app must request all needed scopes in the initial authorization request. Users may grant a subset; the app must check granted scopes via the scope field in the token response and disable features for ungranted scopes. Web server apps DO support incremental auth.
security_constraints.granted_scope_verification: The scope field in the access token response lists ALL scopes granted. Compare against requested scopes. Users may deny individual scopes in granular consent. Disable features for ungranted scopes. The tokeninfo endpoint can also return granted scopes.
security_constraints.user_revocation_behavior: Users can revoke access at https://myaccount.google.com/permissions. Programmatic revocation: POST to https://oauth2.googleapis.com/revoke?token={token}. Revocation removes ALL scopes for the project — all access/refresh tokens for ALL clients under that project become invalid. Revocation may take minutes to fully propagate.

app_setup.app_types: Meta for Developers requires a Facebook App as the identity for any API integration. App types include: Consumer (standard OAuth for individual users), Business (linked to a Business Manager for enterprise features). Instagram Graph API and WhatsApp Cloud API require a Business app type or a consumer app with appropriate product configuration. System users are service-like accounts within Business Manager for server-to-server access.
app_setup.business_verification_triggers: Required when: (a) app requests permissions classified as requiring business verification (most Page/Instagram publishing and messaging permissions), (b) WhatsApp Business API access, (c) app goes into Live mode with certain features. Business verification involves providing legal business documents (tax ID, business license, etc.) and takes days to weeks.
app_setup.app_review_triggers: Triggered when app requests permissions beyond the basic defaults (email, public_profile). App must submit for review with: detailed permission usage description, screencast showing how permissions are used, privacy policy URL, and platform-specific instructions. Review takes days to weeks. Permissions are revoked if app review is not completed within a certain timeframe.
app_setup.development_live_mode: Development mode: App can only be used by users with a Role on the app (Admin, Developer, Tester). All API calls work without app review for these users. Can add up to a certain number of test users. Live mode: App is available to general users. Requires app review for permissions beyond basic. Business verification may also be required.
app_setup.test_users: Can be added in App Dashboard > Roles > Test Users. Test users can authenticate and use the app in Development mode without app review. Useful for development and testing. Limited to a specific count. Test users must have (or create) valid Facebook accounts.

token_matrix.lifetime: Short-lived: ~1-2 hours. Long-lived: ~60 days (obtained by exchanging short-lived token at /oauth/access_token?grant_type=fb_exchange_token).
token_matrix.usage: Authenticates API calls on behalf of a Facebook user. Required to obtain Page tokens and other downstream tokens.
token_matrix.notes: Bearer credential. Store only the long-lived version. Never log raw. Use SHA256 hash for evidence.

token_matrix.lifetime: Short-lived: ~1 hour. Long-lived: never expires (obtained by exchanging a long-lived user token for a Page token).
token_matrix.usage: Authenticates API calls to a specific Facebook Page. Required for Page read, insights, and publishing.
token_matrix.notes: Derived from a user token with pages_show_list or pages_read_engagement permission. Long-lived page tokens do not expire unless the user's access is revoked.

token_matrix.usage: Server-to-server calls that don't require user context (e.g., app-level settings, token inspection).
token_matrix.notes: Form: {app_id}|{app_secret}. Must not be used in client-side code. Limited permissions.

token_matrix.usage: WhatsApp Business API and other business integrations. Represents a system user, not a human.
token_matrix.notes: Requires Business Manager and system user setup. Assigned permissions via Business Manager roles.

token_matrix.usage: Mobile SDK usage only. Limited access scope.
token_matrix.notes: Not applicable for Rig Relay server-side integration.

endpoint_surface_matrix.notes: Read-only Page profile. Requires app review. Business verification likely required.

app_review_matrix.review_triggers: App review is triggered when the app requests any permission beyond public_profile and email. Each permission requires: (a) detailed written description of how the app uses it, (b) screencast demonstrating usage, (c) privacy policy URL, (d) platform-specific instructions. Review takes days to weeks. If review is not passed, permissions are revoked for non-role users.
app_review_matrix.business_verification_prerequisite: Some permissions require business verification before app review can be completed. This includes most publishing/messaging permissions and WhatsApp Business access. Business verification requires submitting legal business documents.
app_review_matrix.testing_without_review: In Development mode, app can be used by users with a Role on the app (Admin, Developer, Tester) without app review. Up to a limited number of test users can be added. This is the recommended path for Rig Relay development.

webhook_security.verification_token: Meta uses a hub.verify_token challenge-response for webhook verification. The app registers a verify token in the App Dashboard. Meta sends a GET request with hub.mode=subscribe, hub.challenge, and hub.verify_token. The app must respond with the hub.challenge value only if the verify_token matches. This prevents unauthorized webhook subscription.
webhook_security.signature_validation: Meta signs webhook payloads with X-Hub-Signature-256 header (SHA256 HMAC using app secret as key). The app must validate the signature before processing any payload. Without validation, an attacker could send forged webhook payloads. The app secret must never be logged or exposed.
webhook_security.appsecret_proof: For Graph API calls, appsecret_proof can be added as a query parameter: appsecret_proof = HMAC-SHA256(access_token, app_secret). This provides an additional security layer and is required for some endpoints. The app secret must never be exposed.
webhook_security.replay_protection: Standard webhook replay concerns apply: an attacker replaying a valid signed payload could cause duplicate processing. Recommended mitigations: (a) track processed webhook event IDs, (b) validate payload timestamps, (c) use idempotency keys where available. Meta docs may provide X-Hub-Signature guidance.
webhook_security.raw_payload_policy: Raw webhook payloads MUST NOT be stored in canonical Rig artifacts. Payloads contain raw message content, sender phone numbers, timestamps, and media URLs. All webhook payloads must be quarantined when received, processed in memory only, and discarded after structured extraction. Never log raw payloads.

whatsapp_constraints.business_account_prerequisites: WhatsApp Business Account (WABA) is required. WABA must be created via Facebook Business Manager. Requires a verified business (business verification). Linked to a Facebook app with whatsapp_business_management permission.
whatsapp_constraints.phone_number_requirements: A phone number must be registered and verified with the WABA. Phone number cannot be used with any other WhatsApp client (personal or business app). Phone number verification via SMS or voice call. The phone number ID is used in API calls.
whatsapp_constraints.message_sending_rules: Messages can only be sent to users who have opted in (messaged first, or opted in via a third-party channel with consent). Outbound business-initiated messages require pre-approved message templates. Free-form messages are only allowed within a 24-hour customer service window after the user's last message.
whatsapp_constraints.template_approval: Marketing, utility, and authentication templates must be submitted to Meta for approval. Templates are reviewed for compliance with WhatsApp Business Policy and Commerce Policy. Rejection reasons include: promotional content violations, formatting errors, missing opt-out language. Templates can take hours to days to approve.
whatsapp_constraints.conversation_windows: 24-hour customer service window: free-form messages allowed. After 24 hours, only template messages are permitted. Conversation-based pricing: conversations are charged per 24-hour session. Different categories: marketing, utility, authentication, service.
whatsapp_constraints.business_verification: Required for WhatsApp Business Platform access. Submit legal business documents. Processing time: days to weeks. Must match business legal name, address, and tax ID. Business verification is separate from app review.

citations.title: OAuth 2.0 for iOS & Desktop Apps
citations.notes: Official Google documentation. Covers PKCE, loopback redirect, refresh token behavior, code verifier/challenge, and desktop app OAuth flow. Confirmed: loopback supported for macOS/Linux/Windows desktop, deprecated for mobile. PKCE with S256 recommended. OOB deprecated.

citations.title: OAuth 2.0 Scopes for Google APIs
citations.notes: Official complete scope reference. Documents all Google API scopes with their sensitivity classification. Sensitive scopes have 'sensitive' indicator in Cloud Console. Non-sensitive scopes: userinfo.email, userinfo.profile, openid. Restricted scopes: drive.readonly, calendar.readonly, contacts.readonly, gmail.readonly.

citations.title: Using OAuth 2.0 for Server to Server Applications
citations.notes: Official service account documentation. JWT-based auth with RS256. Domain-wide delegation requires Workspace super admin, numeric client ID. Can take 24 hours to propagate. Impersonation via 'sub' claim. Covers iat/exp window, key management.

citations.title: Create access credentials — Google Workspace
citations.notes: Official Google Workspace credential setup guide. Covers API keys, OAuth client IDs for all platforms (Web, Android, iOS, Desktop, Chrome Extension, TV), and service account creation with domain-wide delegation setup instructions.

citations.title: OAuth 2.0 Policies
citations.notes: Official OAuth policies. Covers secure credential handling, redirect URI requirements, incremental auth limitations for native apps. Important: installed apps cannot keep secrets, must use PKCE.

citations.title: OAuth 2.0 for Native Apps (RFC 8252)
citations.notes: IETF Best Current Practice for native app OAuth. Establishes PKCE requirement, loopback redirect best practices, and security considerations for apps that cannot keep client secrets.

citations.title: Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) — RFC 7636
citations.notes: Defines PKCE extension to OAuth 2.0. S256 code challenge method using SHA256. Code verifier: 43-128 chars of unreserved characters. Required for native/mobile apps.

citations.title: Meta App Types and Features Reference
citations.notes: Covers Meta app types (Consumer, Business, etc.), development vs live mode, test users, app review triggers, and business verification requirements. NOTE: This URL was not directly accessible via automated fetch; information based on Meta developer platform architecture confirmed via developer community sources. Requires doc verification against current live docs.

citations.title: Meta Permissions Reference
citations.notes: Complete reference for Facebook Login and Graph API permissions. Includes pages_read_engagement, pages_manage_posts, instagram_basic, instagram_content_publish, whatsapp_business_management, etc. NOTE: URL not directly accessible via automated fetch. Permission names and categories confirmed via developer community and Meta platform documentation summaries. Requires doc verification.

citations.title: Instagram Graph API — Getting Started
citations.notes: Documents prerequisites: Instagram Professional/Business Account, Facebook Page linkage, Facebook App configuration, instagram_basic permission. Covers token generation and basic API usage. NOTE: URL not directly accessible via automated fetch. Prerequisites confirmed via developer community. Requires doc verification.

citations.title: WhatsApp Cloud API — Overview
citations.notes: Documents WhatsApp Business Platform prerequisites: WABA, phone number, system user, business verification, message templates, webhook setup. NOTE: URL not directly accessible via automated fetch. Information based on public WhatsApp Business API documentation and developer forums. Requires doc verification.

citations.title: Facebook Graph API Overview
citations.notes: Core Facebook Graph API documentation. Covers token types, versioning, rate limits, permissions model, and common patterns. NOTE: URL not directly accessible via automated fetch. Core API architecture well-documented across developer community.

citations.title: WhatsApp Cloud API — Webhooks Setup
citations.notes: Documents webhook verification (hub.verify_token, hub.challenge), signature validation (X-Hub-Signature-256 with app secret HMAC-SHA256), and payload format. NOTE: URL not directly accessible via automated fetch. Webhook security pattern is standard and well-documented across Meta platforms.

citations.title: Facebook Graph API Rate Limiting
citations.notes: Documents platform rate limits: app-level and user-level rate limiting. Standard rate limits apply per access token. Graph API returns X-App-Usage and X-Ad-Account-Usage headers.

citations.title: Access Token Debugger
citations.notes: Meta provides an access token debugger tool that inspects tokens (type, expiration, scopes, user ID). The corresponding API endpoint is GET /debug_token?input_token={token}&access_token={app_token}. Returns token metadata without exposing the raw token beyond what's needed.

citations.title: OAuth 2.0 Best Practices — Google Identity
citations.notes: Official Google OAuth security best practices. Covers token handling, code verifier usage, state parameter for CSRF protection, and client secret management.

citations.title: Unverified apps — Google Cloud Help
citations.notes: Explains the unverified app warning, app verification process, and how to remove the warning. Test users can bypass the warning during development.

uncertainties: Exact Meta permission names (pages_read_engagement, pages_manage_posts, instagram_basic, etc.) — confirmed via developer community but NOT verified against live Meta developer docs due to bot-blocking on developers.facebook.com. All Meta permission entries marked requires_doc_verification: true with confidence: medium.

Meta app review exact requirements per permission — which specific permissions require business verification as a prerequisite vs. can be reviewed independently. Marked as uncertain in meta_webhook_security and app_review_matrix.

Instagram Graph API: whether Facebook Page linkage is still strictly required or if Instagram Professional Accounts can now work independently via newer API versions. Developer community reports suggest linkage is still required.
WhatsApp Cloud API: exact conversation window behavior (24-hour) confirmed via community docs but needs verification against current WhatsApp Business Policy. Template approval timeline varies.
Google restricted scope security assessment: exact current cost and approved assessor list. Cited as typically $15K-$75K+ but actual cost depends on assessor and scope complexity.

Google Drive metadata.readonly scope: whether it is classified as sensitive or restricted in the latest scope classification. The docs suggest it's sensitive (requires verification but NOT security assessment), while drive.readonly is restricted.

Meta webhook replay protection: exact X-Hub-Signature timestamp handling and recommended replay window not documented in accessible references. Standard webhook replays apply but exact Meta guidance unknown.
Google Admin Directory scopes: exact sensitivity classification and whether they trigger restricted scope assessment. Deferred to enterprise lane regardless.
Meta rate limiting exact thresholds per endpoint — varies by app maturity and access level. Standard headers are provided but exact limits are not publicly documented.
